iconicAnchor.label: IBM corporate design program
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Eliot Noyes, Paul Rand, Charles and Ray Eames, and IBM
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: IBM's program coordinated architecture, products, graphics, exhibitions, and methods of work around a durable modern corporate character.

sources.title: IBM design
supports: IBM established an organization-wide design program spanning architecture, products, graphics, exhibitions, and communications.
The program treated corporate character as a coherent design problem rather than a fixed template.

sources.title: IBM Design Philosophy
supports: IBM explicitly connects its current design approach to modernist methods from Eliot Noyes, Paul Rand, and the Eameses.
The source distinguishes enduring design attitudes from superficial mid-century styling.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches identity system, cross touchpoint, structured type, consistent mark, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/corporate-modernism/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
